Description: Provide leadership with concise workload and aging visibility.
Enable geographic and service-category backlog analysis.
Monitor requests, dispositions, and net request flow over time.
Support filtering, documentation, data-quality handling, and executive-to-detail navigation.
Monitor duplicate and referral patterns using clearly governed definitions and interpretation boundaries.

As an operations leader, I want a concise view of total service-request workload so that I can understand the overall scale of activity before drilling into specific problem areas.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Total Requests KPI is visible for the active filter context.
- With no filters, the KPI reflects the full modeled request population.
- Supported filters update the KPI consistently.

Summary: Identify open backlog aged 90 days or more
Description:
As an operations leader, I want to see how many open requests have aged 90 days or more so that I can identify long-open work that may warrant attention.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Only currently open requests aged at least 90 days are counted.
- The KPI is visible on the executive view.
- Filters recalculate the KPI.
- Documentation labels 90 days as a portfolio monitoring indicator, not an official City SLA.

Summary: Compare open backlog by council district
Description:
As a manager, I want to compare open backlog across council districts so that I can identify geographic concentrations for further investigation.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Open backlog is grouped by council district.
- Relative concentrations are visually identifiable.
- Selecting a district updates applicable KPIs and visuals.

Summary: Identify backlog drivers by service type
Description:
As a department manager, I want to compare backlog by service type so that I can identify service categories contributing most to unresolved workload.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Open backlog is grouped by service type.
- Largest contributors are visually identifiable.
- Selecting a category updates applicable KPIs and visuals.
- Recommendations use investigation language rather than unsupported causal claims.

As an operations leader, I want to compare monthly requests and dispositions so that I can see whether incoming demand and closures are moving in balance.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Both measures appear on the same time axis.
- A selected month can show which measure was higher.
- Both series use the same filter context.

As an operations analyst, I want to view monthly net request flow so that I can identify periods when observed intake exceeds dispositions or vice versa.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Net flow equals Requests minus Dispositions for the same month/filter context.
- Positive and negative months are interpretable using that definition.

Summary: Filter the report by operational dimensions
Description:
As a dashboard user, I want filters to update relevant KPIs and visuals consistently so that I can focus on a specific district, service type, or time period without rebuilding the analysis.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Supported filters update applicable KPIs/visuals.
- Combined filters are honored.
- Clearing filters restores the base view.
- Empty contexts do not present misleading values.

As an analyst, I want metric definitions, assumptions, and limitations documented so that I can interpret results consistently and explain them to stakeholders.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Core measures are defined in plain language.
- Requirements are traceable to stories, capabilities, and UAT.
- Simulated assumptions are labeled.
- Official public-source URLs are provided.

As an analyst, I want blank categorical values represented explicitly as Unknown so that missing categories are visible rather than silently excluded.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Blank values transform to Unknown.
- Unknown remains filterable/groupable.
- The transformation is reproducible on refresh.

Summary: Navigate from executive overview to deeper analysis
Description:
As a reviewer, I want both an executive overview and a deeper analysis view so that I can move from high-level signals to supporting detail efficiently.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Core KPIs and major drivers are visible on the executive page.
- Deeper monthly flow analysis is available.
- Pages use consistent model/filter logic.
- Labels are understandable without specialized DAX knowledge.

As an operations analyst, I want to monitor duplicate and referral rates so that repeated reporting and workflow exits can be identified without confusing them with confirmed physical resolution.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Duplicate Requests uses the documented parent-request relationship.
- Duplicate Rate is visible and responds to supported filter context.
- Referred Requests and Referral Rate are visible using the documented status/indicator logic.
- Referral is described as a workflow exit/transfer rather than proof that the physical issue was resolved.
- Duplicate and referral definitions are documented in the KPI/data dictionary.
